q: What exactly is an off-season rental?
a: It is a furnished summer property let by the month during the months it would otherwise sit empty. In Port Stanley that runs from roughly Labour Day to Victoria Day. You get the same house a summer visitor pays a weekly premium for, at a monthly rate, because the alternative for the owner is an empty building with the heat on.

q: How long is the minimum stay?
a: Thirty nights on most homes. Some owners will take shorter shoulder-season stays in September, October and May — if that is what you need, ask and we will tell you which homes are flexible.

Where utilities are metered separately it is because the home is large enough that winter heating is genuinely unpredictable, and that is disclosed up front rather than in a footnote.

q: What happens if my dates change?
a: Tell us as early as you can. Off-season stays are month-to-month by design, and extending is usually straightforward because the calendar behind you is empty. Shortening depends on the notice you can give and on the individual owner.

q: What is the commute like to St. Thomas or London?
a: Fifteen minutes to St. Thomas and about thirty-five to London, both on paved road with no meaningful traffic. Highway 401 is roughly twenty minutes north. Winter road maintenance in Central Elgin is good — these are year-round routes for the people who live here.

q: Is Port Stanley open in the winter?
a: Partly. Groceries, fuel, the post office, a couple of restaurants and the coffee shops stay open year-round because roughly two thousand people live here regardless of the season. What closes is the summer trade — the patios, the ice cream, the beach concessions. That is the trade you are making, and it is why the rates drop.

q: What do I need to book?
a: Send an enquiry from the listing you want. We come back with availability, the total for your dates, and what the owner needs — usually a signed agreement, a deposit and basic references. Nothing is charged until you have seen the numbers in writing.

q: I own a cottage here. How does listing work?
a: Send us the property using the listing form. Tell us the months you are willing to release and what you want for them, or ask us what the market is paying. We photograph or import your existing listing photos, write the page, and market it to the people already searching for off-season housing in this area.

q: Do I lose my summer calendar?
a: No. We market the off season only. Your July and August stay exactly where they are, on whatever platform you already use. If anything, a well-maintained winter tenant means your place opens in May in better shape than it closed in September.

q: Can I import my existing VRBO or Airbnb listing?
a: Yes, and it is the fastest way to get live. Send us the link and we pull the photographs and the property details straight across, then edit the copy for an off-season audience rather than a summer one. You do not have to re-photograph anything.

q: What does it cost me to list?
a: Nothing up front. We make our money on the bookings we bring you, so if the property does not rent, it has not cost you anything but the time it took to send us the link.

Overwhelmingly people working: travel nurses on hospital contracts, trades on long project bookings, families out of their house for a renovation or an insurance claim, and people between a sale and a closing. They are here because of a job or a deadline, they stay for months rather than weekends, and they are screened before they get your keys.
